NFL.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
NFL.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). LV-NYJ had the model even, so it isn't counted.
NFL.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

NFL.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
NFL.evidence: 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick (NE-CHI at 5.0 and PHI-WAS at 6.2 are the latest). Smaller gaps are mixed: DAL-ARI at 4.2 lost, BAL-BUF at 3.9 won. Overall the over/under is 20-19.
NFL.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

NFL.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
NFL.evidence: In 8 of the 14 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason (DAL-PHI, TB-CAR, NYG-HOU, ARI-LA, CHI-ATL, CAR-PHI, BAL-CLE, ARI-DAL). Turnovers led in NO-NYG and SF-ATL. MIA-NYJ and NE-CHI were close. HOU-JAX had no clear reason.
NFL.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

NFL.lesson: Big-game player picks are close to the model's chances on hit rate, but still lose units.
NFL.evidence: 8 of 25 big-game picks hit, against 8.3 expected, at -7.46 units. The earlier shortfall (5 of 18 against 5.9) has mostly closed. Milestone picks are 20 of 26 against 19.5 expected.
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

NFL.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running below the model's chances.
NFL.evidence: 7 of 16 best-value picks hit this season, against 8.5 expected, at -2.64 units. Several sit only 0.4 to 1.5 points over break-even.
NFL.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

NFL.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
NFL.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.8 for the model against 9.1 for Vegas over 39 graded games. The model is 18-21-1 against the spread (9-4 in week 8). Winners are 25 of 39.
NFL.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

NFL.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
NFL.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts, who was on IR, and DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again, the model had WAS by 3.3 against Vegas -6, and WAS won 27-10: the model's side won, but the spread was lost. Possible case: TB-CAR. Far under 20 games.
NFL.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

NFL.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
NFL.evidence: 9 of 16 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 11.8 expected, at -4.51 units. Overall winners are 25 of 39 (64%).
NFL.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

College.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up; if anything the over hit less often.
College.evidence: Week 8: over hit in 8 of 17 such games. Week 9 so far: 1 of 5 (only Baylor-UCF went over). Combined that is 9 of 22 (41%). I treat the earlier Week 7-8 count of 8 of 13 as overlapping, so I'm not adding it.
College.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: Big misses mostly show up as efficiency gaps; turnovers and finishing drives come second.
College.evidence: Week 8 results: of 25 games missed by 8+ points, efficiency was named first in 15, turnovers in 4, finishing drives in 4, and nothing stood out in 2. Earlier sets showed the same (17 of 24; 12 of 17). Week 9 results had no reviews. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
College.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with the long-run average, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

College.lesson: When the model picks a different favorite than Vegas, results are mixed.
College.evidence: About 4 of 9 right overall as of last run. None of the 9 Week 9 games listed had the model on a different side than Vegas, so there is no new data. Sample is tiny.
College.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

College.lesson: The earlier lean that the favorite fails to cover when the model likes it 3+ points more than Vegas is not settled.
College.evidence: Week 8: favorite covered in 7 of 14 such games. Earlier: 2 of 9. Week 9 so far: 0 of 2 (Tulane, Western Kentucky lost the cover). Overlap between sets can't be confirmed, so I won't total them.
College.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's favorite margin is 3+ points above Vegas's and check the cover rate by size of gap (3-6, 6+). Need 20+ games per group.

College.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak so far.
College.evidence: Season: 6 of 15 hit against 7.6 expected, at -3.55 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed). Fewer than 20 picks. Also, the Coastal Carolina and Temple picks sit oddly against the model's own large margins for the favorites.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: Underdog picks are close to what the model expected, and slightly ahead on units.
College.evidence: Season: 5 of 15 hit against 5.5 expected, at +0.99 units. The early edge came and went. Under 20 picks.
College.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%). Needs 20+ picks.

College.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
College.evidence: Season: 10 of 12 hit against 10.5 expected, at -0.61 units. The prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot. Only 12 picks.
College.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

College.lesson: The model's spread misses are larger than Vegas's over the season.
College.evidence: Season (125 games): average spread miss 12.1 points for the model against 11.2 for Vegas. The gap was 0.9 last run too. Winners right in 80 of 125 (64%) and a 56-64-3 spread record. Week 9 so far: 4 of 9 winners right, 2-7 against the spread.
College.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.
